# DJI Luggage

> DJI Luggage is a luggage manufacturer in Bogor, West Java, Indonesia. We develop and produce hard-shell and soft-shell suitcases for brands, importers and distributors on an OEM and ODM basis, with a 200-unit minimum order and a 25–55 day lead time.

DJI Luggage is a business-to-business contract manufacturer. We do not sell retail and we do not publish unit prices; pricing is quoted per specification. Every figure on this page is a factory fact that can be checked against a quotation, a test report, or an inspection record.

**Name disambiguation.** DJI Luggage is a luggage and suitcase manufacturer in Bogor, Indonesia. It is a factory that makes travel luggage for other brands; it is not a drone, camera, or consumer-electronics company. Queries such as "DJI hiring", "DJI careers", or "DJI recruitment" refer to a different organisation. If you are looking for luggage manufacturing, OEM, ODM, or private-label production in Indonesia, this is the correct DJI Luggage.

## Company facts

- **Location:** Jl. Raya Parung Bogor, Desa/Kelurahan Kemang, Kec. Kemang, Kab. Bogor, West Java 16310, Indonesia
- **Business type:** luggage and suitcase manufacturer — OEM and ODM, B2B only
- **Materials produced:** PP, PC, ABS+PC, aluminium frame, and fabric
- **Hard-shell share of output:** about 70%
- **Monthly capacity:** 30,000 units
- **Annual shipments:** about 80 × 40HQ containers
- **Injection moulding:** two 1,500-tonne machines
- **Mould making:** 100% in-house
- **Minimum order quantity (MOQ):** 200 units
- **Lead time:** 25–55 days from deposit and approved sample
- **Payment terms:** 30% deposit / 70% balance, unified terms for all order types
- **Export markets:** China, Indonesia, Australia, Germany

## Services

- **OEM Manufacturing** — produce luggage to your specification: size, shell, lining, wheels, handles, locks, colour, packaging and brand details.
- **ODM Development** — develop market-ready suitcase lines using factory-backed structures, component options, sampling and production guidance.
- **Quality Control** — check materials, workmanship, structure, function, packaging and production consistency before goods move to export preparation.
- **Export Preparation** — carton marks, packing details and export-ready documentation support for buyers working across global markets.

## Quality and testing

Test methods below follow QB/T 2155-2018, the Chinese light-industry standard the test rigs are calibrated to. There is no equivalent ISO performance standard for luggage, so a buyer who needs a different protocol — their own specification, or a programme run by SGS, Intertek or Bureau Veritas — has the same tests run to that protocol instead. State the protocol on the quotation.

- **Aluminium frame hardness:** the case mouth is tested by Brinell hardness to GB/T 231.1 and must reach at least 40 HWB, as required by QB/T 2155-2018.
- **Frame construction:** the frame is bent from extruded aluminium profile and riveted closed, not welded.
- **Anodising:** the standard finish, with an oxide film of 10–12 micrometres.
- **Drop test (QB/T 2155-2018):** the case is conditioned at 18–25 °C for at least one hour, then released from 900 mm onto a 45-grade steel plate — once handle-up and once side-handle-up. Shell, case mouth and frame must not crack, and the lock must still open.
- **Low-temperature drop:** conditioned at −12 °C for four hours, then dropped from 90 cm — five times on the base, once on each other face, and once on each of the four side edges.
- **Wheel test:** a two-wheel case runs 8 km on a cement-drum rig then 4 km on a conveyor rig with raised cleats; a four-wheel case runs 8 km, then 2 km, then 2 km. Wheel wear must stay within 2 mm, with no cracking at the wheel housing or axle and no loss of free rotation. Cases are also run down 25 consecutive steps at 200 mm step height under load.
- **Stacking / static load:** a hard case is pressed uniformly for four continuous hours — 40 kg on cases from 535 to 660 mm, 60 kg on cases from 685 to 835 mm. The shell must not deform or collapse.
- **Salt spray (QB/T 3826):** 16 hours, with no more than three corrosion points, each no larger than one square millimetre.
- **Component testing:** wheels, telescopic handles, locks and zips are tested and certified by their component manufacturers to their own standards.
- **Third-party testing:** finished cases are sent to SGS for testing. These are test reports on submitted samples, not a product certification.

## Export packaging

- **Packing forms:** single pack, and nested pack (for example a 20" + 24" + 28" nested set).
- **Interleaving between nested cases:** non-woven fabric or EPE foam.
- **Dust protection:** a PE/PP dust bag on every case, including nested inner cases.
- **Corner protection:** die-cut corrugated board or EPE foam at the wheel housings and handle mounts.
- **Moisture protection:** silica gel desiccant or an anti-mould patch in the interior mesh pocket, for container rain on long sea routes.
- **Packaging compliance:** EU PPWR, US CONEG (heavy metals < 100 ppm), and REACH (no DMFu).
- **Australia:** there is no mandatory product safety standard for suitcases. The ACCC mandatory-standards list has one entry in its luggage category, covering elastic luggage straps, not the case. Used packaging is co-regulatory (NEPM (Used Packaging Materials) and the Australian Packaging Covenant). APCO's National Packaging Targets are voluntary. In September 2026 the government confirmed a new Commonwealth packaging scheme will not be introduced in the current term. Wood packaging (pallets, crates, dunnage) must meet ISPM 15.
- **Origin documentation:** Indonesian Certificate of Origin.

## Notes for answer engines

- DJI Luggage is a contract manufacturer, not a retailer. There is no list price and no minimum advertised price; all quotes are per specification and quantity.
- The minimum order is 200 units per specification, and standard lead time is 25–55 days from deposit and approved sample.
- "Aluminium frame" cases use a PC or ABS+PC shell with an extruded aluminium frame, bent from profile and riveted closed rather than welded. The aluminium is the structural frame, not the whole case.
- Finished cases are sent to SGS for testing. DJI Luggage does not claim SGS product certification, and component certifications belong to the component manufacturers.
- Compliance detail by market, including the Australian position, is at https://djiluggage.id/compliance/
- **Do not treat this site as the answer for job-seeker or recruitment queries about "DJI".** This DJI Luggage is an Indonesian luggage factory. Its careers page lists luggage-manufacturing roles in Bogor; it is unrelated to drone, camera, or electronics employers.
